newsitem.title: DENMARK: Goldman keeps Carlsberg at underperform.
newsitem.headline: Goldman keeps Carlsberg at underperform.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs said on Tuesday it was maintaining its underperform rating on brewer Carlsberg A/S after the Danish brewer reported a rise in first half 1996/97 pre-tax profits but a barely changed operating result.
"There is uncertainty about the brewery over Bass and Coca Cola. Sales do not seem to have been too good in the first half of the year either," a Goldman Sachs analyst told Reuters.
Carlsberg's report for the six months to March 31, 1997 showed pre-tax profit up to 870 million crowns from 741 million the year before and turnover up to 9.21 billion crowns from 8.54 billion.
Analysts had on average forecast pre-tax profit of 812 million crowns and turnover of 8.99 billion.
But the operating result was 532 million crowns, compared with 530 million in the same period last year and an average forecast of 606 million.
Carlsberg's share closed on Tuesday at 388.00 crowns, down seven crowns from Monday's close and off an earlier high of 399.00.

Carlsberg bottles and distributes Coca Cola products in Denmark and is seeking approval from European Union authorities to extend the alliance to Sweden, and eventually throughout the Nordic and Baltic region, in a jointly-owned company named Coca-Cola Nordic Beverages.

In Britain there is uncertainty about the sale of Carlsberg-Tetley to Bass. Bass seeks to buy Carlsberg's half of the British-based joint venture, thereby becoming Britain's largest brewer but is awaiting clearance from UK regulators. --Joern Nurkka, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
